contexts.text: Eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage () = their state as to the appropriation of evil and falsity, and the derivative conjunction therewith... To marry = conjunction with evil; and to give in marriage = conjunction with falsity...
A daughter at about her marriageable age is (in that Earth) kept at home...
She is then brought to a house... where (are) many others... who are marriageable...
The love of daughters in their first marriageable age, and also in the second one, is dependent on things coveted from the senses...
He who is in good and weds truth...
(The wives) said that when they came into their marriageable state... they began to love a conjugial life...

By to marry (in the Word) is meant to be conjoined with Heaven in a certain Society of it; and he is conjoined with it in proportion to the intelligence and Wisdom he has acquired for himself in the world from the Lord through the Word...
(The meaning of not having on a wedding garment () shown by experiences in the Spiritual World.) HH 48:end. DP 223:end. SE 4708. SE 5100:6. DMin 4751.
Nuptial feasts (among the ancients) = initiation into conjugial love... For eating and drinking together = appropriation and conjunction.

Eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage () = their state as to the appropriation of evil and falsity, and their consequent conjunction with these... To marry = conjunction with evil; and to be given in marriage = conjunction with falsity. Explained. ( = to conjoin falsity with evil, and evil with falsity. AE 617:31.)

They that were ready went in with Him to the wedding () = that those in good and derivatively in truth are received into Heaven. Heaven is likened to a wedding from the heavenly marriage, which is the marriage of good and truth. ( = conjunction with the Lord by love and faith. AE 252:8.) ( = Heaven and the Church, from the marriage of good and truth. AE 675:6.) AE 840:5.

Can the sons of the wedding-chamber nuptiarum (Greek, numphonos) mourn, so long as the bridegroom is with them? (; ). Those are called sons of the wedding-chamber who are in the truths of the Church and receive good; for the good which is from the Lord is the bridegroom. The reason the sons of the wedding-chamber do not mourn so long as the bridegroom is with them, is that they are in a blessed and happy state while they are in truths conjoined with their good.

That a priest's daughter married to a stranger was not to eat of the heave-offering... () = that the holy things of the Church cannot be appropriated to good which is not conjoined with the truths of the Church.

He who is not in truths is said not to have on a wedding garment. (A wedding garment = Divine truth from the Word. AR 166:3.) ( = faith in the Lord as the Son of God, the God of Heaven and earth, and one with the Father. TCR 380:end) ( = truth from good. SE 5642.) ( = the intelligence of the spiritual man, which is from the Knowledges of truth and good; but he that had not on a wedding garment = a hypocrite, who by a moral life counterfeits a spiritual life, when yet he is merely natural. AE 195:11.)

b. In the Heavens the wedlocks are spiritual, and should not be called wedlocks, but conjunctions of minds from the marriage of good and truth. But on earth they are wedlocks, because they are not of the spirit only, but also of the flesh. And, as there are no wedlocks in the Heavens, the two consorts are not called husband and wife... From this we may know how the Lord's words about wedlocks, in  are to be understood.
The wedding () = the marriage of the Lord with Heaven and the Church by means of the good of love and of faith.
The wedding (of the will and understanding) and its results. Explained.
For the marriage of the Lamb is come () = that from this time there is effected a full marriage of the Lord and the Church. AE 1219.
That there is a wedding of the Church with the Lord. Illustrated.

Blessed are they who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb () = that there is eternal life for those who receive the things of the Lord's New Church. ( = that those will come into Heaven, who by truths from the Word are conjoined with the Lord, and become of the Church, AE 1225.)
The Angel said, Receive these wedding garments. Described. And they were conducted in glory into the New Christian Heaven.
Preliminary remarks about... the wedlocks of Heaven. CL 19.
(A wedding in one of the Heavens. Described.)
As the weddings in Heaven represent the marriage of the Lord with the Church...
But after the wedding, the representation is changed...
As virgins = the Church, the Lord likened it to ten virgins invited to a wedding.
That spiritual nuptials are meant by... after the resurrection they are not given in wedlock (; ; ).

By spiritual nuptials is meant conjunction with the Lord; and this must be effected on earth; and, when it has been effected on earth, it has been effected also in the Heavens, and therefore nuptials and being given in wedlock, do not take place again there. Further explained.
That to perform nuptials = to be conjoined with the Lord; and that to enter into nuptials = to be received into Heaven by the Lord. Illustrated.

The two Angels said, There are nuptials in the Heavens as on earth; but for those only who are in the marriage of good and truth... and therefore it is spiritual nuptials that are meant (in ) These are possible on earth, but not after death, thus not in the Heavens, as is said of the five foolish virgins, who also were invited to the nuptials, but could not enter, because they had not the marriage of good and truth; for they had no oil, but lamps only. Explained.
The three novitiates (were then) full of the hope of nuptials in Heaven.
For the state of sweet delights before the nuptials, is after them (usually) changed into one of indifference.
Those (celibates) who have loved the spiritual things of worship, are given in wedlock, in Heaven.
The sphere of love which goes forth from a wife who is tenderly loved (as perceived by her) husband in the first days after the wedding.
On betrothals and weddings. Chapter.
Thus may conjugial love progress... to the nuptial flame.
That when the period of betrothal is completed, the wedding ought to take place. Explained.

Among customary rites (which are both formal and essential) are weddings (or nuptials); (for) 1. The wedding constitutes the end of the precedent state and the beginning of the subsequent state which is to be inaugurated by marriage, and which is a state of the spirit and the body together... and therefore on that day they put off the state and name of bridegroom and bride, and put on those of married partners... 2. The wedding is an introduction and entrance into a new state, which is, that a virgin becomes a wife, and a youth a husband, and both, one flesh... 3. The wedding is the entering upon the complete separation of the love of the sex from conjugial love... 4. It appears as if the wedding constitutes merely an interposition between these two states, and that it is therefore only a formality which may be omitted; but still there is also in it this essential thing = that the above-mentioned new state is to be entered upon by a covenant; that consent is to be declared in the presence of witnesses; and is also to be consecrated by a priest; besides other things which establish it. As there are essential things in weddings, and as a marriage does not become legitimate until after them, nuptials are celebrated in the Heavens also.
That before the celebration of the nuptials, the conjugial covenant should be ratified in the presence of witnesses. Explained.
That the nuptials should be celebrated with festivity. Explained.
That after the nuptials, the marriage of the spirit becomes one of the body also... Explained.
Nuptial gardens there. Described.

When (the infants in Heaven) arrive at the first age, they are given in wedlock, which is provided by the Lord, and is celebrated in the Heaven where the youth dwells, who presently follows his wife into her Heaven; or into her house, if they are in the same Society.
The change of the virgin state after the nuptials. Explained.
(A full description of a wedding in the Spiritual World. See Marriage.)
The wedding at Cana of Galilee () = the Church among the gentiles.
Her virgins are not wedded () = that the affections of truth have perished through the non-understanding of truth.
(This) appears with all in the first days after the nuptials, when their love emulates love truly conjugial.
